clauses.reason: Item 1 authorizes the Secretaries of the Army, the Navy and the Air Force to issue a citation in the name of the President to any organization, detachment, installation, ship, aircraft or other unit for outstanding performance in action on or after October 16, 1941 (Navy or Marine Corps) or December 7, 1941 (Army or Air Force), and to units of co-belligerent forces. Executive Order 13286 section 74 (68 FR 10619, effective March 1, 2003 under its section 92) added a new section 5 that lets the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating exercise the same authority for the Coast Guard as the Secretary of the Navy has for the Navy and Marine Corps (before: no Coast Guard provision; after: new section 5). Executive Order 14085 section 3 (87 FR 60542, effective on signing, October 3, 2022) amended paragraph 1 by inserting a Space Force case after the words or the Air Force (before: Army or Air Force only; after: the Space Force on or after December 20, 2019). Neither amendment ends the clause, and the Code note prints the order as amended, so it is operative on 2026-10-14.

Item 4 says that the order supersedes Executive Orders No. 9050 of February 6, 1942 and No. 9396 of November 22, 1943. That command was performed when the order took effect: it states no later effective date, so the signing date, January 10, 1957, is used. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note 'Supersedes: EO 9050, February 6, 1942; EO 9396, November 22, 1943' records the same effect. The clause supersedes earlier orders and creates no continuing duty, so it is exhausted by performance; the earlier orders' supersession is not undone. The order's other clauses continue.

research_rationale:
Executive Order 10694 of January 10, 1957 (22 FR 253; held text jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10694.txt, read in full) authorizes the Secretaries of the Army, Navy and Air Force to issue citations in the name of the President to units for outstanding performance in action, sets out the insignia and ribbon rules, and supersedes Executive Orders 9050 and 9396. The held page text is interrupted by the issue's contents and masthead pages and by a running head and a page number, so the machine clauses (which cut item 2 across 7,690 characters of those pages) are replaced by an inventory override of the lead-in, item 1, items 2 and 3 (two spans each) and item 4. Own terms: no clause has an end date or ending condition; item 4 is a one-time supersession exhausted on issuance. Later instruments: Executive Order 13286 section 74 (official text in the packet, effective March 1, 2003 under section 92) added a section 5 for the Coast Guard, and Executive Order 14085 section 3 (official text in the packet, October 3, 2022) amended paragraph 1; both are recorded as later events on item 1. The packet's ACT:EO:10694>EO:12977 lead points to a source-ladder file containing the text of Executive Order 13286, and the held text of Executive Order 12977 does not mention this order, so it adds no instrument. Executive Order 13870 (May 9, 2019) (paragraph (d) of its awards section) refers to citations issued under this order as amended and changes nothing. The Office of the Federal Register catalog note reads 'Amended by: EO 13286, February 28, 2003 | Supersedes: EO 9050, February 6, 1942; EO 9396, November 22, 1943'; the catalog does not list Executive Order 14085, which the Code note and the held text of 14085 show. Current law: current-law:usc has 3 hits (the 10 U.S.C. ch. 57 note printing the order as amended and other Code notes), current-law:ecfr 0 hits. No search or held text revokes or supersedes the order.
